items.title: Stanford Physicist Uses AI to Tackle Quantum Gravity Problem
items.excerpt: Stanford physicist Venkatesa Chandrasekaran proposed a quantum theory of gravity built from light paths and causal diamonds; he says OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra helped develop several calculations and proofs over months of exchanges (~400M tokens). arXiv preprint, not yet peer reviewed.

items.title: Has AI just cracked Internet encryption? Rumoured 'bombshell' stuns scientists
items.excerpt: Several computer scientists suggest on social media that leading AI labs have found AI-generated algorithms that could break public-key cryptography; Nature news weighs the rumour and what it would mean for banking, commerce and privacy.

items.title: Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification
items.excerpt: DeepMind used teams of Gemini 4 agents plus formal verification to optimize well-known quantum algorithms, producing more efficient circuits for modelling fusion energy, chemistry and enzymes on early quantum hardware.

items.title: Scientists Gave AI a 'Stroke' to Map Its Language Circuits
items.excerpt: University of South Carolina researchers deliberately 'injured' LLMs and compared their naming and sentence errors with stroke survivors with aphasia; sorting the model errors by type predicted the patients' patterns of brain damage.

history_match.title: Brain researchers afflict LLMs with 'injuries' similar to those of stroke victims to unpack AI language mechanisms

items.title: Marking an informational text as AI-generated does not influence its ratings, study finds
items.excerpt: In a German online experiment (Applied Psychology: Health and Well-Being), an 'AI-generated' label on nutrition advice barely changed ratings - partly because only ~42% of readers noticed the label at all.

items.title: Smartphone app uses AI to identify illegal wildlife products
items.excerpt: University of Helsinki and IFAW trained ML models on ~40,000 images of wildlife products to recognize items from elephants, pangolins and tigers; a smartphone prototype hit 91.3% accuracy in independent screening (Conservation Biology).

items.title: New modeling tool sheds light on how climate change could reshape marine ecosystems
items.excerpt: A University of Strathclyde machine-learning model trained on decades of Continuous Plankton Recorder data projects copepod abundance on NW European shelf seas falling 58-72% by 2050 under high emissions - steeper than coarse global models (Communications Earth & Environment).

items.title: One random shot or none: A mathematical proof for learning a physical system from one experiment
items.excerpt: Cornell researchers prove a 'zero-one law' in PNAS: for ML models linear in their parameters, if any single experiment can identify a physical system, almost any randomized experiment will too (assuming noiseless, complete measurements).

items.title: EcoVAE: a generative deep learning method for global species distribution prediction
items.excerpt: EcoVAE, a generative variational-autoencoder model, rapidly predicts global species distributions, reveals species associations and flags biodiversity sampling gaps.

items.title: Preventing data leakage in neural decoding
items.excerpt: Data leakage from preprocessing and cross-validation can both inflate and deflate machine-learning neural decoding accuracy; the authors quantify the effect and give guidance for reliable brain-decoding studies.

items.title: Why AI's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is so bittersweet
items.excerpt: A mathematician who wears the Riemann zeta function as a tattoo reflects on why the AI-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis feels like a loss as much as a triumph.

history_match.title: Anthropic mathematician claims to prove Riemann hypothesis, most famous problem in all of math

items.title: A legendary philosopher isn't buying Anthropic's consciousness argument
items.excerpt: Anthropic told investors its AI might be conscious; a prominent philosopher of mind pushes back on the argument and what acting on it would mean.

items.title: A step toward defining the Standard Model on a lattice
items.excerpt: OpenAI describes a candidate nonperturbative lattice definition of the Standard Model and how GPT-6 Astra helped turn the idea into a detailed proof. OFF-LIST domain (openai.com), included for lattice-QCD physics gap.

items.title: Searching for distant planets with Astra
items.excerpt: Two amateur astronomers used Codex and GPT-6 Astra to scan public Kepler and TESS data and flag potential exoplanets; none confirmed yet. OFF-LIST domain (openai.com); exoplanet-candidate hunting is deprioritized.

history_match.title: Claude, find me a planet: amateur astronomers are using AI with mixed results

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 solves two open problems in the physics of black holes
items.excerpt: Anthropic says Claude Fable 5.2 solved two open problems in theoretical physics concerning black holes and the search for quantum gravity. OFF-LIST domain (anthropic.com), vendor claim.
